signal: Today’s strongest signal is that AI progress is moving from opaque end-to-end behavior toward explicit, optimizable contracts: source code can generate RL environments, agent runtimes can snapshot and reclaim resources, execution traces can become structured self-refinement evidence, attention can expose abstention and filtering as separate primitives, and distillation can calibrate away teacher-side noise.

stories.title: CodeMidas turns existing repositories into scalable RL environments for coding agents
stories.summary: CodeMidas uses source code itself as the task-specific input for constructing executable reinforcement-learning environments. Agents explore implemented functionality, infer behavioral specifications, build tests grounded in execution of the original code, and validate candidate tasks through execution checks and repeated solution rollouts. The resulting dataset contains 5,545 tasks from 3,185 open-source codebases across 23 languages and 15 domains; GRPO training of MiMo-V2.5 improved all five evaluated benchmarks, including DeepSWE by 11.7%, ProgramBench by 17%, and Terminal-Bench v2.1 by 8.5%.
stories.whyItMatters: This attacks one of the hardest bottlenecks in coding-agent RL: obtaining diverse tasks with trustworthy verifiers. Instead of depending mainly on issues and commits, any working repository can potentially become a behavioral specification and test generator. For engineering teams, the important pattern is to recover intent from executable behavior, ground generated tests against the original implementation, and scale task creation only after repeated rollout checks eliminate weak or ambiguous environments.
stories.attention: Very high — source code itself can become a scalable supply of verifiable coding-agent RL tasks

stories.title: AWS AgentCore Runtime V2 snapshots agent sandboxes and reclaims memory during sessions
stories.summary: AWS released the next generation of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime, its serverless microVM compute layer for agents. Runtime V2 starts sessions with a small memory profile, allocates memory on demand and reclaims unused memory before the session ends; it also snapshots a prepared agent environment so new instances restore rather than repeat full startup. AWS reports P75 cold starts of 1.9–2.0 seconds for 200 MB to 2 GB images versus 5.4–30 seconds with V1, while retaining scale-to-zero and hardware-enforced session isolation.
stories.whyItMatters: Long-running agents have a runtime cost shape that is different from ordinary stateless APIs: dependency-heavy sandboxes, variable memory use and session isolation can dominate before the model emits a token. Snapshot restore plus live memory reclamation makes those costs explicit infrastructure concerns. Teams should benchmark agent platforms on session churn, image size, memory residency, isolation and recovery behavior rather than treating the model API as the whole serving system.
stories.attention: Very high — managed agent infrastructure is optimizing sandbox startup, memory economics and session isolation as first-class runtime concerns

stories.title: DENSE turns agent execution traces into evidence-grounded shortcut trees for self-refinement
stories.summary: DENSE distills online agent trajectories into nested shortcut trees without requiring post-hoc outcome labels or expert annotations. It compresses redundant attempts, reconciles failures with later recovery evidence, summarizes completed branches and keeps unresolved obligations explicit. On Terminal-Bench 2.1, the authors report the highest strict pass rate among tested non-privileged feedback methods across four recipient models, improving strict pass rate by 7.12–15.64 percentage points from initial executions while using 19.0–43.6% fewer observed recipient tokens on reruns.
stories.whyItMatters: Production agents already generate large volumes of partial successes, failed branches and recoveries; most systems discard that structure or reduce it to a flat summary. DENSE suggests a reusable middle layer between raw traces and retraining: preserve local evidence, mark what is finished, and expose unresolved work to the next attempt. The engineering caution is provenance—recycled lessons should remain linked to the observations that support them so a mistaken interpretation does not become durable agent lore.
stories.attention: High — execution traces can become structured repair knowledge without requiring a separate outcome-labeling pipeline

stories.title: Softmax attention may be missing two primitives: abstention and value-path noise filtering
stories.summary: A new study separates two effects commonly bundled into gated attention. Abstention lets an attention head output effectively nothing instead of being forced to distribute probability mass somewhere, while value-path gating suppresses interference from superposed residual-stream features. In matched 10M-to-350M-parameter models, the benefit of abstention declined with scale while the benefit of filtering increased; the best model at every tested scale included both mechanisms, with negligible parameter overhead and compatibility with KV caching.
stories.whyItMatters: This is useful architectural decomposition rather than another opaque gating trick. If attention heads need both an explicit no-op and a way to reject value-path interference, model designers can reason about those functions independently and test which one scales. The result is still from relatively small models, so frontier-scale validation matters, but the primitives are attractive because they can be introduced without changing the basic serving contract or abandoning the KV cache.
stories.attention: High — separating attention abstention from noise filtering offers a cleaner explanation for why value gating improves pretraining

stories.title: Cal-OPD filters teacher-side deviation before distilling reasoning behavior
stories.summary: Calibrated On-Policy Distillation argues that the token-level discrepancy used by standard OPD mixes two signals: the actual teacher–student capability gap and likelihood shifts caused by the teacher itself, especially when the teacher receives privileged information. Cal-OPD estimates a teacher self-deviation region using positive and negative privileged interventions and optimizes only the discrepancy beyond that region. On mathematical reasoning benchmarks, it retains roughly 52–65% of the original discrepancy signal yet consistently outperforms standard OPD and tested variants across model scales.
stories.whyItMatters: A stronger teacher is not a perfect reference distribution. Blindly minimizing every teacher–student difference can teach the student artifacts created by prompting, privileged context or the teacher’s own uncertainty rather than transferable capability. Post-training pipelines should therefore audit what their discrepancy signal represents and calibrate or mask teacher-side variation before turning it into an optimization target.
stories.attention: High — distillation improves when the training objective separates useful capability gaps from teacher-induced likelihood shifts

takeaway: Design the whole learning-and-execution loop as evidence-bearing infrastructure: derive tasks from executable behavior, benchmark runtime state separately from model tokens, preserve provenance when recycling trajectories, make attention no-op and filtering behavior explicit when architecture allows, and calibrate teacher signals before optimizing a student against them.
